title: The runway has no single address
technology: Distributed venues, public screens, temporary rooms
governingQuestion: What happens when a fashion week is coordinated centrally but staged across a city?
status: evidence-backed draft; recording, named interviews and owner-final approval remain open
hook: There is no single New York runway. The city itself is the switching system.

longform.headline: The runway has no single address
longform.opening: There is no single New York runway. The city itself is the switching system. The evidence reveals a system of coordination rather than a single machine.

sections.heading: Return from digital
sections.copy: The 2021 official schedule marked a return to in-person shows after two predominantly digital seasons and identified CFDA–IMG coordination.

sections.heading: A city of temporary rooms
sections.copy: The September 2026 schedule contains runway shows, presentations, appointments and digital premieres; it coordinates formats rather than naming one venue stack.

sections.heading: Public screens at Rockefeller Center
sections.copy: No public CFDA record reviewed specifies a single technical venue system for New York’s next season; supplier and room-level stacks remain reporting assignments.
